value.body: The Staff Selection Commission (SSC) recruits for Group B and Group C posts in central ministries, departments and organisations — assistants, tax and excise inspectors, auditors, clerks, multi-tasking staff, junior engineers, constables and more. It runs separate exams by qualification level: CGL (graduates), CHSL (Class 12), MTS (Class 10), GD Constable, JE and Stenographer, among others.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: After Class 12 you can apply for CHSL (Lower Division Clerk, Junior Secretariat Assistant, Data Entry Operator), as well as the MTS, GD Constable and Stenographer exams; CGL needs a graduate degree. Each exam has its own age limit with category relaxations. Selection is through computer-based tests and, depending on the post, a typing or skill test and document verification.

value.title: At a glance
items: Posts carry central-government pay scales and benefits; postings can be anywhere in India or within a zone.
Applications run into lakhs per exam, while vacancies are in the thousands.
Exams test reasoning, quantitative aptitude, English and general awareness; CHSL adds a typing or skill test.
SSC publishes a yearly exam calendar, but dates and vacancy counts are often revised.
